question: What is the primary function of carbohydrates in the human body?

options.A: Providing primary energy for daily activities
options.D: Repairing damaged muscle tissues and organs

explanation: Carbohydrates are broken down into glucose, which serves as the body's main and most efficient energy source. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h1)

question: Why is including a wide variety of foods in family meal planning so important?

options.A: It guarantees that every family member eats the exact same calorie count
options.B: It prevents nutrient gaps and avoids excessive intake of any single substance
options.C: It ensures the household spends the maximum possible food budget
options.D: It eliminates the need to provide clean drinking water at meals

explanation: Eating a diverse mix of foods makes it far more likely the body gets all necessary vitamins without relying too heavily on one food type. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h1)

question: Which nutrient is especially critical for adolescent girls and boys during major growth spurts to support expanding blood volume?
explanation: Iron is a core component of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood, making it vital during rapid adolescent growth. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h2)

question: A seventy-year-old patient is losing muscle mass and experiencing bone weakness. Which adjustment is most important to emphasize in their daily meal plan?

options.A: Strict reduction of all dietary fats and oils
options.B: Significantly increased total daily caloric intake
options.D: Higher amounts of protein, vitamin D, and calcium

explanation: Older adults need adequate protein to fight muscle loss and calcium with vitamin D to maintain bone strength despite lower overall calorie needs. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h2)

question: How does buying fruits and vegetables in their natural season help a household manage its food budget?

options.A: Purchasing seasonal items prevents the need to cook meals
options.B: In-season produce is typically more abundant and therefore cheaper
options.C: Out-of-season crops always contain more vitamins
options.D: Seasonal foods require chemical preservatives to stay fresh

explanation: High local supply during harvest seasons drives down the cost of fruits and vegetables while maintaining high nutritional quality. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h3)

question: Which of the following is an effective strategy for reducing household expenditure on proteins without sacrificing nutrition?

options.A: Buying imported specialty protein powders instead of whole foods
options.B: Purchasing single-serving pre-packaged meals from restaurants
options.C: Removing all forms of protein entirely from the family diet
options.D: Replacing expensive meat cuts with plant-based options like beans and lentils

explanation: Plant proteins offer high nutritional value at a fraction of the cost of red meat or poultry. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h3)

question: What is the first practical step a person should take when starting a weekly meal plan?

options.A: Visiting the local market without a list
options.B: Throwing away all existing canned goods
options.C: Ordering takeout food for the upcoming weekend
options.D: Checking current pantry and refrigerator inventory

explanation: Checking what is already at home prevents buying duplicate items and helps build meals around existing ingredients. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h4)

question: Why is batch cooking recommended as part of a family meal strategy?

options.A: It permanently eliminates the need to store food in a refrigerator
options.B: It ensures that all food cooked is consumed in one sitting
options.C: It provides quick, healthy meals for busy days and reduces reliance on fast food
options.D: It allows the cook to avoid washing dishes for an entire month

explanation: Preparing larger portions ahead of time saves valuable time on hectic days and prevents impulsive, less nutritious food choices. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h4)

question: What is the main reason for using separate cutting boards for raw meat and fresh vegetables?

options.A: Complying with modern kitchen aesthetic trends
options.B: Ensuring that the wooden boards dry out faster
options.D: Keeping the vegetable board from smelling like spices

explanation: Using separate boards stops bacteria from raw meat from transferring to foods that will be eaten raw or lightly cooked. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h5)

question: Which cooking method is best for preserving water-soluble vitamins in vegetables?

options.A: Boiling in a large pot for an hour
options.D: Frying deeply in reused cooking oil

explanation: Steaming uses minimal water and short exposure times, preventing valuable vitamins from leaking out into cooking water. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h5)

question: What is the best way to handle a young child who refuses to eat a newly introduced vegetable?

options.A: Offer it repeatedly over time alongside familiar foods without forcing them
options.B: Punish the child by sending them away from the dinner table immediately
options.C: Stop offering all vegetables permanently to avoid any further stress
options.D: Force the child to finish every single bite on the plate before sleeping

explanation: Children often need multiple exposures to a new food before accepting it, and pressure only increases mealtime anxiety. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h6)

question: A family member has newly diagnosed hypertension and requires a low-salt diet. What is the most practical nursing advice for the household cook?

options.A: Prepare two completely different meals every single day for every person
options.B: Stop cooking altogether and buy canned processed foods for everyone
options.C: Add extra salt to the main pot and give the patient plain water
options.D: Cook the base meal with minimal salt and let others add salt at the table

explanation: This approach keeps cooking manageable for the household while protecting the health of the family member with hypertension. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h6)
